chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) disliked exchanging one wasq of the dates of Khaybar for two wasqs of the dates of Medina, because the dates of Medina are inferior of the two.'

key_terms.تَمْرُ الْمَدِينَةِ: Dates from Medina, noted here as inferior in quality
key_terms.تَمْرُ خَيْبَرَ: Dates from Khaybar, known for high quality
key_terms.وَسْق: A specific unit of volume/weight for dry goods, typically around 60 sa's
key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: Disliked (in the context of recommended dislike or caution in trade)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali dislike exchanging Khaybar dates for Medina dates?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) and fairness in commodity exchange, specifically when quality differences are not immediately apparent to the buyer. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often cited to discuss the validity of *mudaraba* or specific trade contracts where one party might exploit information asymmetry regarding the superior quality of Khaybar dates versus the more common Medina dates. It underscores the ethical imperative in Islamic commerce to ensure that exchanges are not merely numerically equal but substantively fair, preventing hidden disadvantages in barter transactions.
